Top 20 Local SEO Experts to Follow in 2025

The top 20 local SEO experts to follow in 2025. Includes thought leaders, consultants, and professionals in local search.

OnwardCraft Team Growth Strategists

Local SEO is the lifeblood of home service businesses. When a homeowner's air conditioner fails in July or a pipe bursts at 2 a.m., they do not browse social media or read a brochure. They pull out their phone, open Google, and search for help nearby. The businesses that appear in the Google Local Pack — that map-powered trio of listings at the top of search results — capture the majority of those emergency calls. The ones buried on page two rarely get a second glance.

The difference between ranking first and ranking tenth often comes down to the quality of your local SEO strategy. And because Google updates its local search algorithms constantly — from the Vicinity update that tightened geographic relevance to the continuous refinement of how reviews, photos, and behavioral signals influence rankings — staying current is not optional. It is a competitive necessity.

That is why following the right voices matters. The best local SEO experts do more than repeat generic advice. They run original experiments, analyze ranking data, test new tactics, and share findings that actually move the needle for service-area businesses. They understand that a plumber in Phoenix faces different challenges than a solar installer in San Diego, and they tailor their guidance accordingly.

This list features the top 20 local SEO experts to follow in 2025. These are practitioners, researchers, educators, and consultants who have demonstrated deep expertise in local search. They publish actionable content, speak at industry conferences, build tools that solve real problems, and consistently help businesses like yours rank higher, earn more visibility, and generate more leads from Google.

Whether you are a contractor, HVAC company, electrician, roofer, or solar installer, following these experts will keep your local SEO knowledge sharp and your strategy ahead of the competition.

How We Selected These Local SEO Experts

Before diving into the list, it is worth explaining how these 20 experts were chosen. The local SEO space is crowded with self-proclaimed gurus who repackage the same basic advice. We wanted to highlight practitioners who genuinely move the industry forward.

Our selection criteria included four factors:

1. Demonstrated Local SEO Expertise Each expert on this list has spent years focused specifically on local search — not general SEO, not content marketing, not paid search. They understand the nuances of Google Business Profile optimization, local pack ranking factors, citation building, review strategy, and service-area business challenges. Their expertise is deep, not broad.

2. Content Quality and Original Research We prioritized experts who publish original research, run experiments, and share data-driven insights rather than opinion pieces. In an industry where misinformation spreads quickly, these voices ground their recommendations in evidence.

3. Industry Recognition and Influence Recognition from peers matters. These experts are frequently cited by other SEO professionals, invited to speak at major conferences like MozCon, LocalU, SMX, and Pubcon, and referenced in industry publications. Their influence extends beyond their immediate following.

4. Active Presence and Accessibility An expert who published one great article in 2019 and disappeared is not helpful in 2025. Every person on this list maintains an active presence through blogs, newsletters, podcasts, social media, or community participation. They are accessible, responsive, and engaged with the local SEO community.

With that framework in mind, here are the top 20 local SEO experts to follow this year.

The Top 20 Local SEO Experts to Follow in 2025

1. Joy Hawkins — Sterling Sky

Joy Hawkins is widely regarded as one of the most influential figures in local SEO. As the founder of Sterling Sky, a local SEO agency serving businesses across North America, and the creator of the Local Search Forum, Joy has shaped how the industry understands Google Business Profile and local pack rankings.

Why Follow: Joy runs continuous experiments on Google Business Profile features, ranking factors, and algorithm behaviors. When Google rolls out a new update or changes how reviews display, Joy is often the first to document the impact with real data. Her annual Local Search Ranking Factors survey, conducted in partnership with Darren Shaw of Whitespark, is the most cited research in the industry. For home service businesses, her insights on service-area business optimization, category selection, and review strategy are indispensable.

Where to Follow: Sterling Sky Blog, Local Search Forum, Twitter/X

2. Darren Shaw — Whitespark

Darren Shaw founded Whitespark, a company that has become synonymous with local SEO tools and citation building. The Whitespark Local Citation Finder and Local Rank Tracker are staples in the toolkits of local SEO professionals worldwide.

Why Follow: Darren combines tool development with deep research. His annual Local Search Ranking Factors study (co-authored with Joy Hawkins) provides the definitive data on what actually moves rankings in local search. He publishes detailed case studies, citation research, and practical guides that help businesses understand exactly how to improve their local visibility. For contractors, his work on citation consistency, review acquisition velocity, and Google Business Profile optimization offers a clear roadmap.

Where to Follow: Whitespark Blog, Twitter/X, YouTube

3. Mike Blumenthal — Near Media

Mike Blumenthal has been studying, writing about, and influencing local search since before Google Maps existed. As the co-founder of Near Media and a longtime columnist for Search Engine Land, Mike brings historical perspective that few can match.

Why Follow: Mike understands the evolution of local search better than almost anyone alive. He tracks Google's local search experiments, documents feature rollouts, and analyzes the business implications of every change. His writing connects technical SEO developments to real-world business outcomes. For home service businesses trying to understand why their rankings shifted or what Google might do next, Mike's analysis is essential reading.

Where to Follow: Near Media, Twitter/X, Search Engine Land Archives

4. Greg Gifford — SearchLab Digital

Greg Gifford is the Chief Search Officer at SearchLab Digital and one of the most entertaining and informative speakers in the local SEO world. His conference presentations are legendary for packing massive amounts of actionable information into fast-paced, visually rich decks.

Why Follow: Greg specializes in local SEO for multi-location businesses and dealerships, but his insights apply directly to home service companies with multiple service areas or branch locations. He breaks down complex local SEO concepts into understandable, implementable steps. His content on Google Business Profile optimization, local link building, and review generation is particularly valuable for contractors looking to scale their local presence.

Where to Follow: SearchLab Blog, Twitter/X, LinkedIn

5. Claire Carlile — Claire Carlile Marketing

Claire Carlile is a freelance local SEO consultant based in the UK who has built a reputation for thorough, practical, and accessible local SEO guidance. She works with businesses of all sizes and is particularly skilled at explaining technical concepts to non-technical audiences.

Why Follow: Claire's blog posts and guides are among the most comprehensive in the industry. She covers everything from Google Business Profile optimization to local schema markup to review strategy with remarkable clarity. For home service business owners who want to understand local SEO without drowning in jargon, Claire's writing is an ideal starting point. Her work on local content strategy and geographic relevance is especially useful for service-area businesses.

Where to Follow: Claire Carlile Marketing Blog, Twitter/X, LinkedIn

Ben Fisher is the co-founder of Steady Demand, a local SEO and Google Business Profile management agency, and a Google Business Product Expert. His deep involvement with Google's product forums gives him early insight into features, bugs, and best practices.

Why Follow: Ben's expertise in Google Business Profile is unmatched. He helps businesses navigate suspensions, optimize listings, understand new features, and troubleshoot problems that can cost leads. For contractors whose livelihood depends on their GBP appearing correctly in local search, Ben's guidance can prevent costly mistakes. How to Learn from These Local SEO Thought Leaders

Following 20 experts can feel overwhelming. Here is how to make the most of their collective knowledge without drowning in information.

Prioritize Based on Your Needs

If you are just starting with local SEO, begin with Claire Carlile and Phil Rozek. Their content is accessible and foundational. If you are dealing with a specific Google Business Profile issue, Joy Hawkins, Ben Fisher, and Colan Nielsen are your best resources. For technical implementation, turn to Tom Waddington. For strategic growth, Mary Bowling and Carrie Hill offer the big-picture perspective.

Engage with Their Communities

Many of these experts are active on Twitter/X and LinkedIn. Following them there gives you access to real-time insights, discussions, and the ability to ask questions. The Local Search Forum, founded by Joy Hawkins, is particularly valuable for getting answers to specific local SEO questions from experts and peers.

Attend Their Events

LocalU conferences, MozCon, SMX, and Pubcon feature many of these speakers. Attending — or watching recordings — gives you access to their latest thinking in a concentrated format. The Q&A sessions at these events often surface insights that never make it into blog posts.

Implement What You Learn

The biggest mistake is consuming content without acting on it. Each expert on this list publishes tactics that can be implemented immediately. Create a system for capturing ideas and scheduling implementation. A single insight from Darren Shaw on citation building or Amanda Jordan on local link opportunities can transform your local visibility.

Why Following Local SEO Experts Matters for Home Service Businesses

The local SEO landscape in 2025 is more competitive than ever. Google's local search algorithms continue to evolve, incorporating more behavioral signals, refining geographic relevance, and raising the bar for what constitutes a quality local presence. The businesses that stay informed and adapt quickly will capture the majority of local search traffic. Those that rely on outdated tactics will fall behind.

For home service businesses — plumbers, HVAC companies, electricians, roofers, solar installers, and contractors of all types — local SEO is not a marketing luxury. It is the primary channel through which emergency and planned service requests are initiated. When a homeowner searches "emergency plumber near me" or "HVAC repair [city]," the businesses in the Local Pack receive the call. The businesses on page two do not.

Following these local SEO professionals ensures you stay ahead of algorithm changes, understand new features as they roll out, and implement strategies that actually work. It helps you avoid costly mistakes — like incorrect GBP configuration, inconsistent citations, or review practices that violate guidelines — and identifies opportunities your competitors are missing.

The experts on this list have collectively helped thousands of businesses improve their local search visibility. Their combined knowledge, freely shared through blogs, forums, social media, and events, represents an unparalleled educational resource. For the cost of your time and attention, you gain access to insights that would cost tens of thousands of dollars in consulting fees.

Building Your Local SEO Knowledge System

To get the most value from following these experts, create a simple knowledge management system:

1. Set Up a Dedicated RSS Feed or Bookmark Folder Collect the blogs of your top five experts in one place. Review them weekly. This prevents the scattershot approach of relying on social media algorithms to surface relevant content.

2. Create an Implementation Log When you read a tactic or strategy that applies to your business, log it. Note the source, the specific recommendation, and the date you plan to implement it. This transforms passive reading into active improvement.

3. Test One Thing at a Time Local SEO is complex, and multiple variables affect rankings. When implementing advice from these experts, change one variable at a time and measure the impact. This disciplined approach helps you understand what actually works for your specific market and business type.

4. Join the Conversation Comment on blog posts, participate in the Local Search Forum, and engage on social media. The local SEO community is remarkably accessible. Asking thoughtful questions often yields detailed, personalized responses from the experts themselves.

5. Share What You Learn When you implement a tactic and see results, share your experience. The local SEO community thrives on real-world feedback. Your insights might help another contractor, and sharing builds relationships that can lead to partnerships, referrals, and collaborative opportunities.

The Future of Local SEO: What These Experts Are Watching

While each expert has their specific focus areas, several trends are dominating local SEO discussions in 2025. Understanding these trends helps you anticipate changes and position your business ahead of competitors.

AI and Local Search

Google's integration of AI into search results — through AI Overviews and enhanced local search features — is reshaping how businesses appear in local queries. The experts on this list are actively studying how AI-generated summaries affect click-through rates, how to optimize for AI-driven local results, and what new opportunities emerge as search interfaces evolve.

Review Generation and Management

Reviews continue to be one of the strongest local ranking factors, and the strategies for generating and managing them are becoming more sophisticated. Experts are exploring video reviews, review response automation, review sentiment analysis, and the integration of reviews across Google's ecosystem.

Service-Area Business Optimization

As Google refines how it handles businesses without physical storefronts, service-area business optimization is evolving. The experts on this list are tracking changes to service area configuration, address handling, and how Google determines relevance for service-area queries. For home service businesses that operate across multiple cities or regions, these developments are critical.

Visual Content in Local Search

Photos and videos are playing an increasingly important role in local rankings and conversion. Google Business Profile photo optimization, video content strategy, and visual user-generated content are areas where early adopters are gaining significant advantages.

Local Schema and Structured Data

The technical foundation of local SEO continues to advance. Schema markup for local businesses, services, reviews, and FAQs helps search engines understand your business and can enhance how you appear in search results. Experts like Tom Waddington are pushing the boundaries of what structured data can accomplish for local visibility.

Conclusion

Local SEO is not a set-it-and-forget-it discipline. It requires continuous learning, testing, and adaptation. The 20 experts featured in this list represent the best minds in local search — practitioners who combine deep expertise with a willingness to share what they know.

For home service businesses, following these local SEO thought leaders is one of the highest-return investments you can make. The insights you gain will help you rank higher in local search, attract more qualified leads, and build a sustainable competitive advantage in your market.

Start by following the experts whose focus aligns most closely with your current challenges. Engage with their content. Implement their recommendations. Track your results. Over time, you will build a local SEO program that consistently delivers the visibility and leads your business needs to grow.

The local search landscape will continue to evolve. Algorithm updates, new features, and changing consumer behaviors will create new challenges and opportunities. By staying connected to the experts who are shaping the industry, you ensure your business is never caught off guard and always positioned to capitalize on what comes next.
